title: In Situ Nucleation and Growth Mechanisms of Tellurium Nanoribbons via van der Waals Epitaxy
content: Mechanistic understanding and control over the growth of one-dimensional (1D) nanostructures is essential for their utilization in devices, where small changes in growth mode strongly impact structure, morphology, and inherent quantum confinement effects that are important for (opto-)electronic, quantum computation, and energy storage/conversion applications [1,2]. Direct in situ visualization of growth with high spatial and temporal resolution allows understanding of the self-assembly and growth mode of 1D nanostructures beyond what is possible via post-growth analysis [3–5]. Tellurium (Te), a narrow-bandgap semiconductor with an intrinsically chiral structure [6,7], is an example of an emerging 1D material exhibiting strongly orientation-dependent properties such as piezoelectricity, thermoelectricity, and photoconductivity [8,9]. To realize the full potential of its intriguing anisotropic and chiral properties, the synthesis of high-quality 1D Te nanostructures with controlled structure, alignment, and handedness is crucial [10].
